fixes.explanation: That's it, baker. Solomon, David's son and Israel's king, rebuilds the cities Hiram had given him and settles Israelites there (2 Chronicles 8:2). Somebody handed him a fixer-upper and he went straight to work. Me, I got handed a junk drawer once, and I spent my time welcoming the newcomers.

Nice thought, friend, but the text goes another way. It says Solomon rebuilds the cities Hiram had given him and settles Israelites there (2 Chronicles 8:2). Hiram was king of Tyre (2 Chronicles 2:3). Nothing in this verse has Solomon handing the cities back.
Not these cities, friend. Solomon rebuilds them and settles Israelites there (2 Chronicles 8:2). Falling apart sounds like my old drawer with all its dust, and that's NOT where this story goes.
True, baker. The text says Solomon went to Hamath-zobah and captured it (2 Chronicles 8:3). Short verse, big result. Solomon goes, and the city is captured.

Not quite, friend. The text says Solomon conscripted these descendants who remained in the land to be forced laborers (2 Chronicles 8:8). Sending them out of the land isn't what the verse says. This is a heavy part of the story, so I'll say it plainly.

That's not what the text says, baker. Solomon conscripted these people to be forced laborers, as they are to this day (2 Chronicles 8:8). The verse says nothing about land being given to them. It's a heavy verse, and I think it hurts a little to read.

That's the one, baker. Solomon didn't consign any Israelites to slave labor, because they were his men of war, the leaders of his captains, and the commanders of his chariots and cavalry (2 Chronicles 8:9). Men of war, captains and commanders of chariots. That's a lot of titles to fit on one team.

That's him, baker. Hiram sent Solomon ships captained by his servants, along with crews of experienced sailors (2 Chronicles 8:18). Hiram is king of Tyre (2 Chronicles 2:3), the same Hiram who gave Solomon those cities (2 Chronicles 8:2). Looks like he's a generous neighbor.

She doesn't show up in this passage, friend. The text says Hiram sent Solomon ships captained by his servants, along with crews of experienced sailors (2 Chronicles 8:18). Hiram is the king of Tyre (2 Chronicles 2:3) who also gave Solomon cities (2 Chronicles 8:2).

Yes, baker. They went to Ophir and acquired 450 talents of gold, which they delivered to King Solomon (2 Chronicles 8:18). A talent is a big weight, so that's a LOT of gold. Hiram also sent crews of experienced sailors with those ships.

Cedar does come up in Solomon's story, like when he asks Hiram for cedar logs (2 Chronicles 2:3), but not here. The text says they went to Ophir and acquired 450 talents of gold (2 Chronicles 8:18). So the blank is gold.

Horses are in this passage, since Solomon has cities for his chariots and horses (2 Chronicles 8:6). But the text says the ships to Ophir acquired 450 talents of gold and delivered it to King Solomon (2 Chronicles 8:18). So the blank is gold, not horses.
